BBC News explainer - SUGGESTED ONE TO READ (opened and read in full). LD datePublished = dateModified Wed 14 Oct 20:52 BST. By Tom McArthur.
LD headline: 'Ukraine war: Why is Starlink internet so important on the battlefield?' (front page runs it as 'Why is Starlink internet so important on the battlefield in Ukraine?' - re-headlined without republishing).
Using Starlink, Ukrainian drones maintain stronger connections with operators over longer distances than conventional radio and are less vulnerable to jamming.
George Barros, Director of Innovation and Open Source Tradecraft, Institute for the Study of War (ISW), to the BBC: Starlink is 'the backbone of military communications in Ukraine', used across Kyiv's naval, land and air forces. Restrictions could have major implications as the technology allows 'drones, artillery and command posts to function as a single real-time network where the time between sensor-to-shooter is minimized.'
DECISIVE NUMBER: Shahed drones fly at speeds in excess of 198mph, so a 100mph (160km/h) throttle makes Ukrainian efforts to chase them down 'all but impossible'. Per ISW, throttling at this relatively low speed makes interception of jet-powered Russian drones 'all but useless'.
Tom Whittington, electronic warfare expert and associate fellow at RUSI, to BBC Radio 4's PM programme: the satellite system lets Ukraine move large amounts of data - video, text, voice - as smartphones do but without the infrastructure phones need. The speed restrictions 'effectively preclude' anything connected to the network going above 100mph, making drone navigation difficult within Ukraine and Russian-occupied territory inside Ukraine.
INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE GUARDIAN'S CAVEAT: 'Starlink does not work inside Russia, but Ukrainian drones can use the satellites to communicate back to their operators during strikes. There is no ready replacement for the network.'
Musk's full X post as quoted by the BBC: 'Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS. Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company.'
Musk says Starshield and Starlink are separate but 'in many cases they share the same underlying satellite technology'.
Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory. Earlier this year Musk cut the use of Starlink terminals for Russian forces, blunting Moscow's advance and causing confusion among Russian commanders.
Trump has criticised Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries and called for a new leader - criticisms echoed by Musk.
